subject: AWS Marketplace: SKU routing + sandbox activation checklist
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@aws-marketplace.amazon.com>, Amy Chen <amy@acmecloud.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace: SKU routing + sandbox activation checklist

Hi Evan / Amy,

Thanks again for the call this morning. This thread will track the operational checklist to get AcmeCloud live on AWS Marketplace (SaaS metering + fulfillment). We want to be sure the SKU routing/entitlement mapping and a sandbox activation are done before procurement signs.

Key asks from our side:
- Sandbox activation for AcmeCloud tenant (sample account: acme-sbx-01) so we can end-to-end test metering events and entitlement callbacks.
- Confirm the SKU routing table expectations (per-customer SKU vs. global SKU fallback).
- Shared schema for metering events and webhook payloads (we attached schema-mapping.xlsx).
- DocuSign route for the SaaS contract amendment + MOP (link in Drive).

I've attached a draft mutual action plan and a quick SKU routing diagram (sku-routing-diagram.png) — they should help frame implementation tasks. Proposed timeline:
- Week 1 (this week): Sandbox enabled, sample metering events accepted.
- Week 2: Entitlement verification + fulfillment callbacks verified.
- Week 3: Go/no-go & procurement counter-signature.

Please confirm who's owning the AWS-side webhooks and whether Acme wants per-customer SKUs or a single SKU with entitlement mapping. If you prefer, we can provision a short canary window (50 subs) rather than full production immediately.

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: schema-mapping.xlsx (xlsx), mutual-action-plan.pdf (pdf), sku-routing-diagram.png (png)
From: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@aws-marketplace.amazon.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Chen <amy@acmecloud.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: SKU routing + sandbox activation checklist

Thanks Diego — got it.

Short answers up front: we can enable a sandbox tenant for metering tests within 48 hours. On SKU approach, AWS Marketplace prefers a single SKU per product with entitlement-level mapping for most SaaS sellers (easier on catalog + entitlement reconciliation). That said, per-customer SKUs are allowed if you have invoicing/finance reasons to segment.

Action items from our side:
- Evan: Provision sandbox and provide test credentials (will send separate email with creds).
- AWS integration team: Confirm webhook signing mechanism and example payloads.
- Acme: Confirm whether they need per-customer SKUs for billing reconciliation.

I reviewed schema-mapping.xlsx quickly — it looks fine but we will send a version with the marketplace-specific fields (customerIdentifier, entitlements[].startDate, meteredQuantity) flagged.

We'll also include a short runbook for retry/backoff semantics on webhook delivery.

Evan Shaw
Manager, AWS Marketplace Integrations
avail: +1-206-555-0142

Diego / Evan / Amy — adding a couple of internal ops items to keep procurement and finance in sync: 

1) Procurement needs the final SKU approach documented (single SKU + entitlement mapping vs. per-customer SKUs) by EOD Tuesday so they can finalize the billing hook in the SaaS amendment.
2) Marissa — can you own the DocuSign route once Evan confirms the sandbox? I'll need the signed amendment before we flip production.
3) For audit: please capture sample webhook payloads and a signed acknowledgement that Acme stores minimal PII in metering events. AWS, please flag fields that are PII-sensitive.

Marissa, Diego — let's capture an acceptance checklist for the sandbox tests:
- Metering event accepted (true) and returned with 200 in under 2s
- Entitlement verification flow returns expected plan_id mapping
- Fulfillment callback triggers activation in Acme tenant
- Negative tests: duplicate metering events are deduplicated

I'll loop in Finance once we have the final mapping. Evan — appreciate the runbook on retry semantics; we'll match our SDK's retry behavior to that.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Perfect — thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifications and next steps: 

1) Acme confirmed they prefer single SKU + entitlement mapping (Amy: per your finance team's ask, this keeps catalog simpler).
2) Evan: please send sandbox credentials and the marketplace-annotated schema by end of day so our QE can start tests tomorrow morning.
3) Marissa: please prepare the DocuSign envelope for the SaaS amendment; include the acceptance checklist Kimberly listed as an appendix. I'll route to Acme procurement once sandbox tests are green.

Acceptance criteria reminder (for the thread):
- Sandbox accepts metering events and responds 200 within 2s for happy path
- Entitlement lookup in fulfilment returns plan mapping (plan_id -> internal_tier)
- Fulfillment callback activates the customer license in Acme tenant
- Retry/backoff behavior documented and tested for 5xx/429 responses

I'll open a shared Drive folder with test accounts and sample payloads (link above). Evan, Amy — once we have the creds I will schedule a 30-minute canary test window (we'll keep it to 20-50 subs).

Diego
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
